verses.text: Lowkey, before anything even existed, God started the whole thing from scratch—the skies, the earth, literally everything.
Back then, the earth was just empty vibes—no shape, straight pitch-black darkness covering the deep water, and God's Spirit was just hovering over the waves.
Then God said, "Bet, let there be light," and instantly, light pulled up.
God saw that the light was good, so he separated the light from the darkness.
God named the light Day and the darkness Night. Evening came, morning followed: day one.
Then God said, "Let there be open space between the waters, splitting the waters apart."
God made that open space and separated the water below it from the water above it. And that is what happened.
God named the open space Sky. Evening came, morning followed: day two.
Then God said, "Let the water under the sky gather in one place, and let dry land show up." And it happened.
God named the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters Seas. God saw that it was good.
God said, "Let the earth grow green plants: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees that carry seeds in their fruit, each kind reproducing its own kind." And it happened.
The earth brought up grass, seed-bearing plants of each kind, and fruit trees with seeds, each kind reproducing its own kind. God saw that it was good.
Evening came, morning followed: day three.
Then God said, "Let lights appear in the sky to separate day from night. Let them mark seasons, days, and years,
and shine from the sky over the earth." And it happened.
God made the two great lights: the brighter light to rule the day, and the dimmer light to rule the night. He made the stars too.
God placed them in the sky to shine over the earth,
to govern the day and the night, and to separate light from darkness. God saw that it was good.
Evening came, morning followed: day four.
Then God said, "Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the open sky."
God created the huge sea creatures and every living thing moving through the water, each kind, and every bird with wings, each kind. God saw that it was good.
God blessed them: "Have plenty of young, multiply, and fill the seas. Birds, increase across the earth."
Evening came, morning followed: day five.
Then God said, "Let the earth bring out living creatures of every kind: livestock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals." And it happened.
God made the wild animals, the livestock, and every creature that moves along the ground, each kind. God saw that it was good.

Then God said, "Let's make humankind in our image, reflecting who we are. Let them rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, the whole earth, and every creature that moves across it."
God created humankind in his own image; in God's image he created them—male and female he created them.

God blessed them and said, "Have children, grow in number, fill the earth, and bring it under your care. Rule over the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and every living thing moving on the earth."
God said, "Look, I'm giving you every seed-bearing plant across the whole earth and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. They will be your food.
And to every animal on land, every bird in the sky, and every creature moving along the ground that has life, I'm giving every green plant for food." And it happened.
God looked at everything he had made, and it was very good. Evening came, morning followed: day six.
